I've had a smart lock on my front door for five or six years now, and I've tried quite a few models. For most people, the ULTRALOQ Bolt Fingerprint is a solid choice because it supports Apple Home, has built-in Wi-Fi, and offers a wide variety of ways to unlock it. Whether you prefer using your fingerprint or entering a PIN, you'll be covered.

HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips, and all things related to Apple's smart home framework.

Apple Home support, but no Home Key

ULTRALOQ says the Bolt Fingerprint is its first fully Apple Home-integrated smart lock, and honestly, that's what drew me to it. I still miss Touch ID on my iPhone. You can lock and unlock via the Home app or Siri, and if you have a HomePod or Apple TV set up as a home hub, you can add it to automations and scenes just like any other Apple Home accessory—and control it from anywhere too.

One thing I noticed is still missing for me, though: Home Key support. If you could just tap your iPhone or Apple Watch to get in, this lock would be perfect. That's the one thing holding it back, but it's not a deal-breaker.

I'm hoping ULTRALOQ adds it in the next model, because with Home Key, this lock would go from good to near-perfect. It's also compatible with Amazon Alexa, Google Home, SmartThings, and IFTTT, so no matter which smart home platform you prefer—or even if you switch in the future—you're covered. It uses 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi rather than Bluetooth, so basic remote control via its app doesn't require an extra bridge.

More unlocking methods than you'll ever use

The Bolt Fingerprint offers a really generous range of unlock options. The fingerprint reader can store up to 50 fingers along with 50 codes. You can unlock it from your phone's app, have it unlock automatically as you approach the door, or use Siri, Alexa, or Google Assistant for voice control. Two physical keys are included in the box, so you won't get locked out if the batteries die. For me, a smart lock without a physical key backup is a non-starter.

You can set up to 50 custom codes and generate one-time or time-limited codes for friends, guests, or cleaners. If you rent out your home, that feature alone is worth the price of admission.

There's also a Lockout Mode that temporarily disables all electronic access methods, including codes and app access. It's genuinely useful for anyone going on holiday who wants extra peace of mind while the house is empty. I never expected a smart lock to have that feature, but it's a nice bonus.

Installation and adding to Apple Home

I've installed more smart locks over the past few years than I can count, so the process is pretty second nature to me at this point. With the right tools on hand, it takes about ten minutes. If you're swapping in a new deadbolt, there's no wiring or drilling required. All you need is a Phillips screwdriver, though you'll want to replace the strike plate on the door frame too.

Once you scan the lock into your Apple Home setup and assign it to a room, you can control it through the Home app, or add it to automations and scenes that trigger multiple actions at once—like having the lights turn on the moment the door unlocks.

Wrapping up the ULTRALOQ Bolt Fingerprint

Overall, if you don't need Home Key support, the ULTRALOQ Bolt Fingerprint is a really solid choice. In day-to-day use, fingerprint unlock quickly becomes the method you rely on most. Installation is straightforward too. I've been using it on my office door for a while now, since I often have laptops sitting there waiting to be shipped out, and I wanted an extra layer of security. I love how it automatically unlocks as I approach, and I can keep track of who's come and gone. The fingerprint recognition takes me right back to the days of Touch ID.

You can pick up the Bolt Fingerprint directly from Amazon or the ULTRALOQ website.
